question: When was Jesus rejected by the people in his hometown of Nazareth?
summary: Luke 4:13-30 places the Nazareth rejection at the very *beginning* of Jesus' Galilean ministry, immediately after the temptation, as the inaugural event setting the trajectory of his mission. Matthew 13:53-58 and Mark 6:1-5 place the same Nazareth rejection much later, after the Sermon on the Mount / parable discourse, well into the public ministry. The same incident — Jesus rejected in his hometown — appears at incompatible points in the narrative chronology.

reconcile.connective: JFB holds this was Jesus' one and only Nazareth visit, the very scene Luke narrates, against the majority-harmonist two-visit view.

discrepancy.connective: Bart Ehrman argues Luke deliberately relocated Mark's midpoint Nazareth episode to the ministry's opening for theological effect, not literal chronology.

excerpts.excerpt_text: This, according to the majority of Harmonists, was the second of two visits which our Lord paid to Nazareth during His public ministry; but in our view it was His first and only visit to it.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly names the harmonist debate over whether Matthew/Mark's Nazareth episode is a distinct second visit or the very event Luke narrates first — the crux of the chronological-placement tension.
excerpts.source_note_text:
And when he was come into his own country--that is, Nazareth; as is plain from Mar 6:1. See on Joh 4:43, where also the same phrase occurs. This, according to the majority of Harmonists, was the second of two visits which our Lord paid to Nazareth during His public ministry; but in our view it was His first and only visit to it. See on Mat 4:13; and for the reasons, see Luk 4:16-30.
Whence hath this man this wisdom, and these mighty works?--"these miracles." These surely are not like the questions of people who had asked precisely the same questions before, who from astonishment had proceeded to rage, and in their rage had hurried Him out of the synagogue, and away to the brow of the hill whereon their city was built, to thrust Him down headlong, and who had been foiled even in that object by His passing through the midst of them, and going His way. But see on Luk 4:16, &c.
